work.title: The First Part of Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 4, Scene 7
scene.title: SCENE VII. Another part of the field.

content.text: Alarum. Excursions. Enter old Talbot led by a Servant.

lines.text: Where is my other life? Mine own is gone.
lines.plainText: Where is my other life Mine own is gone

lines.text: O, where's young Talbot? Where is valiant John?
lines.plainText: O where's young Talbot Where is valiant John

lines.text: Triumphant Death, smear'd with captivity,
lines.plainText: Triumphant Death smear'd with captivity

lines.text: Young Talbot's valour makes me smile at thee.
lines.plainText: Young Talbot's valour makes me smile at thee

lines.text: When he perceived me shrink and on my knee,
lines.plainText: When he perceived me shrink and on my knee

lines.text: His bloody sword he brandish'd over me,
lines.plainText: His bloody sword he brandish'd over me

lines.text: And like a hungry lion did commence
lines.plainText: And like a hungry lion did commence

lines.text: Rough deeds of rage and stern impatience;
lines.plainText: Rough deeds of rage and stern impatience

lines.text: But when my angry guardant stood alone,
lines.plainText: But when my angry guardant stood alone

lines.text: Tendering my ruin and assail'd of none,
lines.plainText: Tendering my ruin and assail'd of none

lines.text: Dizzy-ey'd fury and great rage of heart
lines.plainText: Dizzyey'd fury and great rage of heart

lines.text: Suddenly made him from my side to start
lines.plainText: Suddenly made him from my side to start

lines.text: Into the clustering battle of the French;
lines.plainText: Into the clustering battle of the French

lines.text: And in that sea of blood my boy did drench
lines.plainText: And in that sea of blood my boy did drench

lines.text: His over-mounting spirit; and there died
lines.plainText: His overmounting spirit and there died

lines.text: My Icarus, my blossom, in his pride.
lines.plainText: My Icarus my blossom in his pride

lines.text: O my dear lord, lo where your son is borne!
lines.plainText: O my dear lord lo where your son is borne

content.text: Enter soldiers, with the body of young Talbot.

lines.text: Thou antic Death, which laugh'st us here to scorn,
lines.plainText: Thou antic Death which laugh'st us here to scorn

lines.text: Anon, from thy insulting tyranny,
lines.plainText: Anon from thy insulting tyranny

lines.text: Coupled in bonds of perpetuity,
lines.plainText: Coupled in bonds of perpetuity

lines.text: Two Talbots, winged through the lither sky,
lines.plainText: Two Talbots winged through the lither sky

lines.text: In thy despite shall scape mortality.
lines.plainText: In thy despite shall scape mortality

lines.text: O thou whose wounds become hard-favour'd Death,
lines.plainText: O thou whose wounds become hardfavour'd Death

lines.text: Speak to thy father ere thou yield thy breath!
lines.plainText: Speak to thy father ere thou yield thy breath

lines.text: Brave Death by speaking, whether he will or no;
lines.plainText: Brave Death by speaking whether he will or no

lines.text: Imagine him a Frenchman and thy foe.
lines.plainText: Imagine him a Frenchman and thy foe

lines.text: Poor boy, he smiles, methinks, as who should say,
lines.plainText: Poor boy he smiles methinks as who should say

lines.text: Had Death been French, then Death had died today.
lines.plainText: Had Death been French then Death had died today

lines.text: Come, come, and lay him in his father's arms;
lines.plainText: Come come and lay him in his father's arms

lines.text: My spirit can no longer bear these harms.
lines.plainText: My spirit can no longer bear these harms

lines.text: Soldiers, adieu! I have what I would have,
lines.plainText: Soldiers adieu I have what I would have

lines.text: Now my old arms are young John Talbot's grave.
lines.plainText: Now my old arms are young John Talbot's grave

content.text: Enter Charles, Alençon, Burgundy, Bastard, La Pucelle and forces.

lines.text: Had York and Somerset brought rescue in,
lines.plainText: Had York and Somerset brought rescue in

lines.text: We should have found a bloody day of this.
lines.plainText: We should have found a bloody day of this

lines.text: How the young whelp of Talbot's, raging-wood,
lines.plainText: How the young whelp of Talbot's ragingwood

lines.text: Did flesh his puny sword in Frenchmen's blood!
lines.plainText: Did flesh his puny sword in Frenchmen's blood

lines.text: Once I encounter'd him, and thus I said:
lines.plainText: Once I encounter'd him and thus I said

lines.text: "Thou maiden youth, be vanquish'd by a maid."
lines.plainText: Thou maiden youth be vanquish'd by a maid

lines.text: But with a proud majestical high scorn
lines.plainText: But with a proud majestical high scorn

lines.text: He answer'd thus: "Young Talbot was not born
lines.plainText: He answer'd thus Young Talbot was not born

lines.text: To be the pillage of a giglot wench."
lines.plainText: To be the pillage of a giglot wench

lines.text: So, rushing in the bowels of the French,
lines.plainText: So rushing in the bowels of the French

lines.text: He left me proudly, as unworthy fight.
lines.plainText: He left me proudly as unworthy fight

lines.text: Doubtless he would have made a noble knight.
lines.plainText: Doubtless he would have made a noble knight

lines.text: See, where he lies inhearsed in the arms
lines.plainText: See where he lies inhearsed in the arms

lines.text: Of the most bloody nurser of his harms.
lines.plainText: Of the most bloody nurser of his harms

lines.text: Hew them to pieces, hack their bones asunder,
lines.plainText: Hew them to pieces hack their bones asunder

lines.text: Whose life was England's glory, Gallia's wonder.
lines.plainText: Whose life was England's glory Gallia's wonder

lines.text: O, no, forbear! For that which we have fled
lines.plainText: O no forbear For that which we have fled

lines.text: During the life, let us not wrong it dead.
lines.plainText: During the life let us not wrong it dead

content.text: Enter Sir William Lucy and a French Herald.

lines.text: Herald, conduct me to the Dauphin's tent,
lines.plainText: Herald conduct me to the Dauphin's tent

lines.text: To know who hath obtain'd the glory of the day.
lines.plainText: To know who hath obtain'd the glory of the day

lines.text: On what submissive message art thou sent?
lines.plainText: On what submissive message art thou sent

lines.text: Submission, Dauphin! 'Tis a mere French word.
lines.plainText: Submission Dauphin 'Tis a mere French word

lines.text: We English warriors wot not what it means.
lines.plainText: We English warriors wot not what it means

lines.text: I come to know what prisoners thou hast ta'en,
lines.plainText: I come to know what prisoners thou hast ta'en

lines.text: And to survey the bodies of the dead.
lines.plainText: And to survey the bodies of the dead

lines.text: For prisoners ask'st thou? Hell our prison is.
lines.plainText: For prisoners ask'st thou Hell our prison is

lines.text: But tell me whom thou seek'st.
lines.plainText: But tell me whom thou seek'st

lines.text: But where's the great Alcides of the field,
lines.plainText: But where's the great Alcides of the field

lines.text: Valiant Lord Talbot, Earl of Shrewsbury,
lines.plainText: Valiant Lord Talbot Earl of Shrewsbury

lines.text: Created for his rare success in arms
lines.plainText: Created for his rare success in arms

lines.text: Great Earl of Washford, Waterford, and Valence,
lines.plainText: Great Earl of Washford Waterford and Valence

lines.text: Lord Talbot of Goodrig and Urchinfield,
lines.plainText: Lord Talbot of Goodrig and Urchinfield

lines.text: Lord Strange of Blackmere, Lord Verdun of Alton,
lines.plainText: Lord Strange of Blackmere Lord Verdun of Alton

lines.text: Lord Cromwell of Wingfield, Lord Furnival of Sheffield,
lines.plainText: Lord Cromwell of Wingfield Lord Furnival of Sheffield

lines.text: The thrice victorious Lord of Falconbridge,
lines.plainText: The thrice victorious Lord of Falconbridge

lines.text: Knight of the noble Order of Saint George,
lines.plainText: Knight of the noble Order of Saint George

lines.text: Worthy Saint Michael, and the Golden Fleece,
lines.plainText: Worthy Saint Michael and the Golden Fleece

lines.text: Great Marshal to Henry the Sixth
lines.plainText: Great Marshal to Henry the Sixth

lines.text: Of all his wars within the realm of France?
lines.plainText: Of all his wars within the realm of France

lines.text: Here's a silly stately style indeed!
lines.plainText: Here's a silly stately style indeed

lines.text: The Turk, that two and fifty kingdoms hath,
lines.plainText: The Turk that two and fifty kingdoms hath

lines.text: Writes not so tedious a style as this.
lines.plainText: Writes not so tedious a style as this

lines.text: Him that thou magnifiest with all these titles
lines.plainText: Him that thou magnifiest with all these titles

lines.text: Stinking and fly-blown lies here at our feet.
lines.plainText: Stinking and flyblown lies here at our feet

lines.text: Is Talbot slain, the Frenchman's only scourge,
lines.plainText: Is Talbot slain the Frenchman's only scourge

lines.text: Your kingdom's terror and black Nemesis?
lines.plainText: Your kingdom's terror and black Nemesis

lines.text: O, were mine eye-balls into bullets turn'd,
lines.plainText: O were mine eyeballs into bullets turn'd

lines.text: That I in rage might shoot them at your faces!
lines.plainText: That I in rage might shoot them at your faces

lines.text: O, that I could but call these dead to life!
lines.plainText: O that I could but call these dead to life

lines.text: It were enough to fright the realm of France.
lines.plainText: It were enough to fright the realm of France

lines.text: Were but his picture left amongst you here,
lines.plainText: Were but his picture left amongst you here

lines.text: It would amaze the proudest of you all.
lines.plainText: It would amaze the proudest of you all

lines.text: Give me their bodies, that I may bear them hence
lines.plainText: Give me their bodies that I may bear them hence

lines.text: And give them burial as beseems their worth.
lines.plainText: And give them burial as beseems their worth

lines.text: I think this upstart is old Talbot's ghost,
lines.plainText: I think this upstart is old Talbot's ghost

lines.text: He speaks with such a proud commanding spirit.
lines.plainText: He speaks with such a proud commanding spirit

lines.text: For God's sake, let him have them; to keep them here,
lines.plainText: For God's sake let him have them to keep them here

lines.text: They would but stink and putrify the air.
lines.plainText: They would but stink and putrify the air

lines.text: Go, take their bodies hence.
lines.plainText: Go take their bodies hence

lines.text: I'll bear them hence;
lines.plainText: I'll bear them hence

lines.text: But from their ashes shall be rear'd
lines.plainText: But from their ashes shall be rear'd

lines.text: A phoenix that shall make all France afeard.
lines.plainText: A phoenix that shall make all France afeard

lines.text: So we be rid of them, do with them what thou wilt.
lines.plainText: So we be rid of them do with them what thou wilt

lines.text: And now to Paris in this conquering vein.
lines.plainText: And now to Paris in this conquering vein

lines.text: All will be ours, now bloody Talbot's slain.
lines.plainText: All will be ours now bloody Talbot's slain
